title: Sales By Representative has a Sales Type filter, all selected
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • You are signed in as a user with the "Admin" role at {Location-A}.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • Starting screen: Reports > Sales By Representative is open in a desktop browser at least 1024 px wide.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Open the Sales Type filter.
  2. Read the filter's label with all options selected.
  3. Untick Part Sales.
  4. Untick Labor and Parts too.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: three options in this order: "Labor", "Parts", "Part Sales"; all three are selected.
  • Step 2: it reads "Sales Type: All".
  • Step 3: it reads "Sales Type: Labor, Parts"; Part Sales rows leave the report and the totals and counts follow.
  • Step 4: it reads "Sales Type: None" and the report shows its empty state with no invoices.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Splitting Sales Representatives", Confluence 919928833, version 10 (19 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 20 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10890, story SV-11272 (Story 8, Filter both sales reports by Sales Type)

  • S8-R1: “Sales By Representative has a "Sales Type" filter with three options, in this order: "Labor", "Parts", "Part Sales". All three are selected by default.”
  • S8-R2: “Any combination can be selected. Rows, summary rows, totals and invoice counts follow the selection (S5-R10 to S5-R12).”
  • S8-R3: “With all three selected the filter reads "Sales Type: All". With none it reads "Sales Type: None". Otherwise it reads the selected names in option order, for example "Sales Type: Labor, Parts".”
  • S8-R5: “With no option selected the report includes no invoices and shows its empty state.”
